newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now on a visit to the United States, has invited U.S. investors to Bangladesh, saying the country offers the world's "cheapest" labour and access to a market of two billion people in south and south-east Asia.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationslist Party (BNP) has alleged the government was "conspiring" to give India the "corridor" in the name of Asian Highway, and warned of launching a "people's movement" against such a move.
Bangladesh has signed the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty (CTBT). Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina signed the treaty in New York on Thursday.

Retired army colonel Abdur Rashid, self-confessed killer of of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, is now staying in Libya, said his wife. Rashid fled the country shortly after Awami League took office in late June.

Bangladesh might have to wait for some more time for foreign investors coming in a big way as they would watch the country's next political development before making fresh commitment, said Gill James, an economist with the Standard Chartered Bank.
Bangladesh on Friday began its surgarcane crushing season, setting a production target of 215,000 tonnes of sugar during the 1996-97 fiscal year (July-June).
